_about: The narration of the Noncredit Summit film's narrated cut, draft 1 (S335 SkyMotion, 2026-10-05). Sam, 2026-10-05: "do one version with just music and another with voice over from our ElevenLabs narrator. See if we have access to a female voice with a slight hispanic accent." One to three plain sentences a scene, written from the deck's slide scripts (CPLBrain 20261005_Noncredit_Summit_CPL_Slides_1.md), every figure the film's: 52,394 served (said as more than fifty-two thousand), 7,500 a year by 2030, one in four, 29,649 (said as nearly thirty thousand), the 34% worded as the deck's .md gives it, 8 and 8.5 and 22 units, 21 colleges, 78% at 28 colleges, 49 at 253 sites, $35 million and $2 million, $50,000 grants, $1.8 million. Funding vocabulary: funding, max award; never earn for an institution, money or pool. The voice says the figures in words and writes MAP as map, so the captions and the aligner read what she says; the captions write MAP back.

engine.name: elevenlabs
engine._why: ladypatty1 is an ElevenLabs library voice: "a deep, warm millennial female voice with a soft, soothing tone and a subtle Mexican accent". Sam picked her by ear from three candidates on 2026-10-05 (S335: "Let's go with Ladypatty"), over Carli and Lilith. A library voice's owner can withdraw it, so the clips are committed here and a re-read needs the voice still listed (creative_list_voices). Sierra is the name the CPL Initiative's films give their narrator (Sam, 2026-10-02, on the funding film). One generation per scene through the ElevenLabs connector; Nadia was read twice, because the first read swallowed the A in CompTIA A plus (whisper gave it probability 0.00) and said 'at' as 'and', and the second names the certification first. narrate.py brings every clip to -20 dBFS speech RMS, as the funding film's Sierra.

layout._why: The funding film's narrated pacing: each scene is its lead-in (the seam, its barrier and the first reveal), its clip, and its air.

scenes.text: Hi, I'm Sierra. Here's how noncredit learning becomes college credit.

cues.why: the name beneath the lockup, Narrated by Sierra
the title, Noncredit learning, college credit, letter by letter

scenes.air_why: The title's picture runs 5.7 s past its first letter (the letters, the subtitle, the seam), and the voice names the title 2.4 s into the scene; without the air the clip fills the scene and the name and title would lead their words by 1.7 and 2.3 s.

scenes.text: Last year, Chancellor Christian said that noncredit and not-for-credit learners would be key to our CPL goal. Our colleges have served more than fifty-two thousand students through CPL so far. By twenty thirty, CPL for about seventy-five hundred noncredit learners a year is within reach.

cues.why: her 2025 words, word by word
the goal track and its label, students served through CPL
the count landing on 52,394
the line Within reach by 2030: CPL for about 7,500 noncredit learners a year

scenes.text: About one in four of our students takes a noncredit course each year. Nearly thirty thousand students earned a noncredit award in twenty twenty-four to twenty-five. And noncredit students who were working before they enrolled saw their median quarterly wages rise thirty-four percent a year after finishing or leaving their program.

cues.why: the first figure, 1 in 4
the count landing on 29,649

cues.word: And noncredit students who were working
cues.why: the third figure, +34%, and its line

scenes.text: Mira's free noncredit community health worker courses at Cabrillo College mirror credit courses. She earned eight units of credit and a Certificate of Achievement without retaking a class.

cues.why: the first step, the mirrored courses

scenes.air_why: The path's last step, the note under the portrait and the footnote follow the certificate by 3 s of picture, and the voice ends 1.6 s after naming it; without the air the gold step and the certificate lead their words by 1.0 s.

scenes.text: Carla climbed Mount San Antonio College's noncredit health ladder to the LVN license. College of the Desert awards twenty-two units for that license toward an associate degree in nursing, and Mount San Antonio College is documenting its own ladder now.

scenes.text: Nadia is finishing a noncredit IT support certificate at North Orange Continuing Education. Her A plus certification from CompTIA already carries credit at twenty-one colleges, and North Orange is building her path to an associate degree.

cues.why: the first step, the noncredit certificate
the second step, Google IT Support and CompTIA A+
the fourth step, the credit certificate and associate degree

scenes.air_why: The note under the portrait (CompTIA A+ at 21 colleges) and the footnote follow the last step, and the voice ends as it names the step; without the air the last step leads its words by 1.4 s.

scenes.text: Faculty have already said yes. At twenty-eight colleges, seventy-eight percent of eligible EMT units reach a transcript, and forty-nine statewide credit determinations sit ready at two hundred fifty-three college sites. Most of the opportunity is still ahead.

scenes.text: The state budget provides thirty-five million dollars one-time and two million ongoing for CPL. Last year, fifty-thousand-dollar grants went to three noncredit programs. This year, one point eight million dollars in noncredit funding reaches every community college noncredit program. Credit and noncredit FTES together size every max award.

the line one-time, and $2 million ongoing
the card Last year, $50,000 grants
the card This year, $1.8 million
